turns.answer:
At HCM 2026, guest minister Victor Adeyemi taught extensively on the anointing of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing its role in imparting supernatural capacity and divine abilities, and the necessity of developing spiritual maturity and character to effectively steward these gifts.

He explained that when the Spirit of the Lord comes upon a person, it gives them supernatural capacity [4]. This anointing imparts supernatural and divine abilities, enabling believers to operate supernaturally rather than naturally [5][7]. Citing the example of David, upon whom the Spirit of the Lord came from the day he was anointed (1 Samuel 16:13), Victor Adeyemi highlighted that this anointing can transform one's life, taking them from obscurity to leadership—from "the backside of the desert...to shepherding God's people," and from "prison...to the palace" [4]. The Holy Ghost is presented as the key to increase and enlargement, imparting divine endowments and spiritual gifts [7]. He further illustrated this with Joshua, who was filled with the spirit of wisdom, which encompasses knowledge, understanding, and skill, imparted through Moses (Deuteronomy 34:9) [8][9]. The Holy Spirit is interested in every area of a believer's life and is ready to help them do everything excellently [8].

Victor Adeyemi stressed that while the anointing comes upon a life, believers must develop the capacity to receive and use it effectively, requiring cooperation with the Holy Spirit [5]. One crucial way to activate God's active presence and experience spiritual refreshing is through praying in the spirit [6][11]. He recounted personal experiences of sustained prayer in the spirit before ministering, noting that it causes God's manifest presence to become very active [6][11][15][16]. He also shared how asking the Lord for "rain in the time of the latter rain" can lead to "bright clouds and showers of rain," which manifests as an overflow of the Spirit, symbolizing spiritual blessing and impartation [1][14].

He emphasized that God intends to use the entire body of Christ in the supernatural, not just a select few special individuals [18]. This includes the manifestation of miracles such as healing from various ailments like dental problems, lumps, asthma, and ulcers, as well as deliverances, even for those connecting online [1][10][17][18]. Beyond gifts for ministry within the church, the Holy Spirit imparts abilities for vocational callings, such as supernatural generosity in giving (Romans 12) [9].

However, Victor Adeyemi underscored that spiritual gifts must be balanced with character. He taught that one's charisma should never take them to a place their character cannot sustain them [16]. Leadership, as seen in Psalm 78:72, requires both the "integrity of heart" (character) and the "skillfulness of hands" (charisma or gifts) [16]. He encouraged believers to exercise themselves in virtues like love, forgiveness, patience, longsuffering, goodness, meekness, and temperance, recognizing that through the Holy Ghost, they can do these supernaturally even when it seems impossible naturally [13]. Developing the capacity for God's plans requires spiritual maturity [13].

At HCM 2026, guest minister Victor Adeyemi's evening session focused on deepening the understanding of the anointing of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing the impartation of supernatural capacity and divine abilities, and the essential development of spiritual maturity and character to effectively steward these gifts. He had indicated earlier that more would be discussed about supernatural capabilities and measures in the spirit "in the evening" or "tonight" [1].

Victor Adeyemi taught that when the Spirit of the Lord comes upon a person, it gives them supernatural capacity [1]. This anointing imparts supernatural and divine abilities, enabling believers to operate supernaturally rather than naturally [2][7][18]. He used the example of David, upon whom the Spirit of the Lord came from the day he was anointed (1 Samuel 16:13), transforming his life from obscurity to leadership—from "the backside of the desert...to shepherding God's people," and from "prison...to the palace" [1][17]. The Holy Ghost is presented as the key to increase and enlargement, imparting divine endowments and spiritual gifts [7]. He further illustrated this with Joshua, who was filled with the spirit of wisdom, which encompasses knowledge, understanding, and skill, imparted through Moses (Deuteronomy 34:9) [3][18]. The Holy Spirit is interested in every area of a believer's life and is ready to help them do everything excellently [18]. This means carrying out one's job or business not by might nor by power, but by the Spirit of the Lord [6].

He stressed that while the anointing comes upon a life, believers must develop the capacity to receive and use it effectively, which requires cooperation with the Holy Spirit [1][2]. Spiritual maturity is crucial; he explained that as long as one remains a "child in the things of the spirit," they will be "under tutors and governors," but when they grow into maturity, God can place things in their hands [8]. This growth involves developing a strong spirit, spiritual senses, and discernment, as "strong meat belongs to them who are of age" (Hebrews 5:14) [8]. He admonished believers to "exercise thyself unto godliness" (1 Timothy 4:7-8) and "put away childish things" [8]. Victor Adeyemi deeply emphasized the importance of character, stating that one's charisma should never take them to a place where their character cannot keep them [9]. While the anointing brings gifts and graces, it is faithfulness in that anointing and strong character that lead to accessing greater measures of the spirit [9]. He shared a personal testimony of experiencing arrogance after a powerful anointing early in his ministry and how he immediately fell on his face to plead with the Lord, asking that any miracle or use of him that would lead to pride or losing his mind should never happen [13][15]. From that day, he deliberately exercises himself unto humility, recognizing that the Holy Spirit is an embodiment of the fruit of the Spirit, and believers must exercise themselves in humility, love, forgiveness, patience, and other virtues through the Spirit [12][15]. God has not called us to live possible lives, but supernaturally, and we must develop capacity for what God has in store for us, maturing spiritually for the grace our destinies require [12].

He also touched on how to activate God's active presence. While God is everywhere and within us, His active presence can be brought into manifestation through prayer in the spirit, which is fellowship with God [16]. He illustrated this by recalling how, when Israel went out of Egypt, God's manifest presence caused the sea to flee and Jordan to be driven back (Psalm 114:1-8), demonstrating how obstacles will move out of the way when God's presence is active [16].

Rev. Peter's messages, as provided in these segments, do not mention Bitcoin or cryptocurrency investing.

However, he does offer teaching on wealth, finances, and how a believer should approach money and opportunities:

*   **Money is not inherently evil** Money itself does not have a character of its own; it takes after the character of the person who owns it and what they do with it [2]. If money is used for evil, it becomes evil, and if obtained through wrong means, it will negatively impact one's life. Conversely, getting money righteously allows one to remain a righteous person [2]. Rev. Peter encourages believers not to be afraid of being rich or becoming multi-billionaires, even having private jets or global companies, as this is within God's will [1].
*   **Trust in God, not money** Rev. Peter emphasizes that placing faith in money is a misplaced trust. He states that if you believe having more money will make your life better, you have already put your trust in the wrong place [4]. The solution to problems is found in the knowledge of God and the ability to trust Him, not in money [7]. There are many things God can do in your life without money, such as buying property or a car, because "the whole world is his" (Psalm 24:1) [7].
*   **The Holy Spirit is the number one form of wealth** Rev. Peter teaches that the leading of the Holy Spirit is the primary form of wealth and what distinguishes believers from unbelievers in business and career [3]. Following the "inward witness" can make you rich, even when instructions may not immediately make sense, because God sees what you don't [3]. Divine leading positions you where good things are coming, so things come to meet you rather than you running after them [3].
*   **Sensitivity to the Holy Spirit in finances** A primary factor in how faith works in the area of finances and material things is your sensitivity to the leading of the Holy Spirit and what He is asking you to do [8][9]. It is crucial for someone in need to hear what God is saying, not just what people are saying [9].
*   **God's plan for wealth creation** God is raising a wealthy people from among believers. There are openings of opportunities for wealth, openings of your eyes to recognize these opportunities, and openings of your understanding to maximize them [6].
*   **Faith and financial growth** Faith does not grow; it is the believer who grows in faith [5]. It's important to let God set your faith targets, as the faith of God is not obligated to fulfill personal ambitions [5]. Rev. Peter recalls using the "same faith" for small needs in university as for thousands of dollars later, illustrating that the capacity of faith is there, but growth is in the individual [5]. He encourages being open to possibilities of bigger things, like having "bulk money," and shares testimonies of significant financial enlargement far surpassing initial targets when open to God's word [13].
*   **Materialism vs. being led by the Spirit** Materialism is not about having wealth, but when material things drive your life, determine your choices, and are placed above God. A Christian life should be led by the Spirit, not by money [18].
*   **Obedience for prosperity** Prosperity is largely tied to your ability to listen and obey God (Deuteronomy 28:1) [17]. If God is not Lord over your money, you cannot expect Him to prosper you more [17].

turns.answer:
Rev. Peter Alabi does not endorse specific candidates for elections, emphasizing that the choice of who to vote for is a personal one guided by your conviction and God's Word [6][11][13].

He teaches that the church is not a political party and its primary assignment is not to build roads or engage in political campaigns [2][5]. While the church recognizes government officials, Rev. Peter has stated he will not give his microphone to politicians to address the congregation, to prevent the church from becoming a political campaign ground and corrupting its calling [1].

As a believer, it is your divine obligation to vote in elections, and not doing so means you have no right to complain or pray about governance [3][9]. However, your vote should not be swayed by sentiments, food, or money [9][11]. Rev. Peter encourages you to evaluate candidates based on their plans for Nigeria, ensuring they are intelligible and visible, rather than just offering false hopes [9].

Beyond simply voting, Rev. Peter advises Christians to actively participate in the electoral process. Getting your Permanent Voter's Card (PVC) is a first step, but more importantly, he encourages joining a political party to infiltrate the system and build long-term influence [4][8][13][18]. He teaches that it is godly to be in politics and not a sin for a Christian to participate [18]. For those with political ambitions, he advises thinking long-term and patiently building up influence, suggesting that winning elections means moving from winning arguments to taking action, starting small, as God does big things by starting small [4][13].

Rev. Peter also stresses the importance of how Christians conduct themselves regarding political choices. He advises against fighting with people, whether online or physically, over who they choose to vote for, warning against losing covenant relationships over politics [7]. He teaches that you cannot bully people to like your preferred candidate, and calling someone a "devil" for not supporting your candidate is akin to witchcraft [11]. Instead, Christians should tolerate others' political leanings [11].

Once a candidate wins and is sworn into office, they are considered a "minister of God" (Romans 13:1), and believers are to be subject to their authority [6][16][18]. Therefore, it is important to pray for whoever wins, because there are spiritual realities and demonic influences over regions, and leaders need prayer to exercise God's agenda for the betterment of people [14]. Rev. Peter cautions against cursing your country or its leaders, emphasizing that Nigeria is a blessing and we should bless it [15][18]. He also advises against putting absolute confidence in politicians, stating that in a democracy, the president is chosen by the will of the people, not directly by God, to avoid blaming God for administrative outcomes [10][15][16].

Rev. Peter also mentioned a "civic ecclesia" event where the church would discuss governance and politics in the light of God's word, including whether a Christian should participate in politics [11].

The provided messages do not contain any information about Rev. Peter's thoughts on Pastor Adeboye's teaching on holiness. Rev. Peter teaches on holiness in several messages, focusing on its nature and how it relates to believers [1][4][6][8][11].

Here's what Rev. Peter teaches about holiness:
*   In **Sunday Special Ministration**, Rev. Peter teaches that holiness is primarily our nature and being before it becomes our doing. He states that the same holiness and capacity found in God's nature that makes Him stand out is inside believers. He emphasizes that "as He is, so are we in this world," meaning believers are exactly like Him now [1][4] (1 John 4:17, 2 Peter 1:4).
*   In **Midweek Service**, Rev. Peter declares that believers are "holy already" and that this holiness is a calling to live holy. He says, "I love righteousness, I hate iniquity," and explains that what is true of Jesus is true of believers, leading them to win by doing things the right way and converting others to Christ [3].
*   In **The Believers Authority Over Darkness**, Rev. Peter explains that believers have "fruit unto holiness," which is the life God has called them to, encompassing holiness in thought, affection, desires, and passions. He states that God has given believers power and authority over sin, and they should speak God's word when tempted [5].
*   In **Followers of Christ - Part 5**, Rev. Peter asserts that it is easier for believers to live holy than unholy because holiness is in their nature. He encourages believers to allow themselves to walk in holiness, as their new nature is pleasing to God, though their actions can still displease Him [6][7].
*   In **Right About Turn - Spiritual Home Training Series Part 1**, Rev. Peter teaches that one of a pastor's duties is to show believers the difference between what is common and what is holy. He explains that holiness means to be uncommon and not found anywhere else, highlighting that there must be a difference in how believers conduct themselves, even in worship, compared to the world [8].
*   In **The Book of Colossians (The JESUS-Only Epistle) - Part 1**, Rev. Peter states that holiness is not primarily about behavior but a state into which God has called believers through salvation. He explains that believers are holy because they have been "set apart for God," and this state of holiness then births the conduct of holiness [11].
*   In **Psalms, Doctrine and Spiritual Songs**, Rev. Peter emphasizes that God has already made believers holy. He quotes Romans 12 about presenting bodies as a "living sacrifice, holy and acceptable," noting that our bodies have already been made holy [15].

The provided messages do not explicitly address what the Catholic church teaches about purgatory.

However, Rev. Peter teaches about the state of the departed in the context of prayer, emphasizing that believers should pray for themselves rather than relying on deceased relatives. He states that "there is no dead relative in heaven that is praying for you" and stresses that it is "dangerous to just be repeating things of the spirit without checking in the word of God whether they are true or not" [15].

From other messages, Rev. Peter proclaims that God is a preserver, declaring there shall be "no loss" and "no sorrow" for believers [4]. He also ministers life to overcome any "hidden death" in the body, spirit, or soul, including fear, and encourages staying in the Word to silence the fear of death, declaring, "You shall not die... but you shall live" (Psalm 36:9) [1]. He emphasizes that the reborn spirit inside a believer has eternal life and does not want to die, encouraging excitement about living and the future God has planned [12].

Pastor Funlola Alabi adds that God is merciful and does not want us to die in sickness, even if it's due to our own doing. She explains that God will heal and correct His children in His own way, not through affliction or disease [17].

turns.answer:
Heritage of Faith Church teaches that faith is ultimately about trusting God and acting on His Word, not just believing. Here's what Rev. Peter and Pastor Funlola teach about faith:

*   **RFC 2025 - Day 1 Evening - Things Not to Put Your Faith in - 1** Rev. Peter emphasizes that the object of your faith must always be God and nothing else, encouraging believers to trust in the Lord with all their heart (Proverbs 3:5-6) and to repent if they find their heart trusting in something else [1]. He teaches that faith is synonymous with trust, and that your confessions of faith are backed by your belief in God [1].
*   **Our Heritage of Faith 1** Rev. Peter defines faith as putting your trust in God and acting on His Word [10]. He highlights Abraham's example, who obeyed God's call to go out because he believed and acted on the Word of God (Hebrews 11:8) [8]. He clarifies that faith is not merely belief, because "even the devils believe also and they tremble" (James 2:19), but it is to believe and then act on what you believe [8].
*   **The Call of GOD - Part 1** Rev. Peter stresses that believers are called to trust God completely, not man, themselves, their boss, or investments [5]. He states it is impossible to be stranded as a called person who is trusting God [13].
*   **RIGHTEOUSNESS - The Gift of No-Condemnation - Part 4** Rev. Peter teaches that the faith we use to please God (Hebrews 11:6) is the "God kind of faith" that God Himself supplies, and that Jesus is the author and finisher of this faith (Hebrews 12:2) [7]. He explains that God is a "faith God" who speaks and expects manifestation [7].
*   **HCM 2025** Pastor Funlola Alabi teaches that as believers, we already have the capacity to believe God and should use that capacity [2]. She encourages boldness and action, noting that believing God doesn't cost anything; it only requires trust [2].
*   **Faith Essentials** Pastor Funlola Alabi distinguishes between natural human faith, which is based on observation and experience, and the "God kind of faith" which comes only by the Word of God and operates in Him [6]. She states that not all people have the faith of God, but all believers do [6].
*   **Prayer Works** Rev. Peter leads the congregation in confessing to walk by faith, take steps of faith, and that every prayer is a prayer of faith, believing that nothing formed against them shall prosper [3].

turns.answer:
Rev. Peter teaches that God has no problem with believers being rich, but He does have a problem with covetousness [1].

Here's what Rev. Peter says about money:
*   In **Day 24 - Evening Session**, he emphasizes that understanding how faith works is crucial for supernatural finances and financial breakthroughs. He explains that a primary factor in how faith works with finances is sensitivity to the Holy Spirit's leading on what to do [1][4]. He also says God doesn't have a problem with us being rich, but with us being covetous [1].
*   In **GOD's Principle of Faithfulness 8 - Ambidextrous Believers Part 21**, Rev. Peter tells believers not to be afraid of being rich, even multi-billionaires with private jets and global companies, because it is the will and plan of God [5].
*   In **GOD's Principle of Faithfulness 6 -Ambidextrous Believers Part 19**, he explains that a good church talks about money, but not louder or differently than Jesus did. He warns against the extreme of materialism where everything is about money, and states that gain is not godliness, meaning godliness is not measured by material things [6]. He also notes that 1 Timothy 6 instructs on our attitude towards money, specifically warning against supposing that gain is godliness [6].
*   In **New Creation Realities**, he teaches that a Christian's attitude towards money should be one of stewardship, recognizing that the money belongs to God, not to them. He states that if you have been bought with a price, whatever belongs to the "slave" belongs to the "owner" [7].
*   In **Inclined Part 1**, he reiterates that believers are stewards, not owners, of the money in their possession. He states that thinking as an owner prevents prosperity and that faithfulness in stewardship leads to God entrusting more [8].
*   In **Day 23**, he emphasizes that giving is an obligation for believers, encouraging generosity in the local church, referring to it as partnership in the New Testament. He suggests giving a portion of what God has prospered you with, and encourages not doing less than a tithe [9].
*   In **No One Is Exempted - Giving Series Part 2**, Rev. Peter teaches about the discipline of saving money, not for a "rainy day," but because it is the right thing to do and good discipline. He references Jesus commending the poor widow who gave her two mites as offerings to God, highlighting that it's not about the amount but the heart behind the giving [10].
*   In **GOD's Principle of Faithfulness 7 - Ambidextrous Believers Part 20**, he explains that money itself does not have a character, but takes after and amplifies the character of its possessor. He quotes 1 Timothy 6:10, stating that the love of money, not money itself, is the root of all evil [11].
*   In **HCM 2025**, he teaches that God does not service poverty but destroys it, by working on believers' thinking. He encourages believers to be free in their spirits to prosper, as it is not a crime to be rich from honest means. He also stresses that there is a spiritual and physical side to victory in finances, and the aim of the spirit of poverty is to keep you from doing God's will [12][13].
*   In **New Year Immersion Service**, Rev. Peter explains that the Word of God teaches the character and disposition a believer should have towards money in marriage, emphasizing no love of money, generosity, and accountability as a steward [14].
*   In **GOD's Principle of Faithfulness 3 - Ambidextrous Believers Part 16**, he teaches that the Bible's guidance on money in marriage focuses on attitude: stewardship, recognizing God owns the money, and generosity. He advises cutting down debts and saving money to build capacity for opportunities [15].
*   In **Day 16**, he shares a personal testimony of growing in knowledge and understanding to manage his own finances. He emphasizes that believers must learn how to get finances and release faith for things, and that sufficient knowledge and understanding allow one to "collect by yourself" rather than relying on others to meet needs [18].

Rev. Peter teaches that prayer is a means to release and access the power that believers already possess through faith in Jesus Christ, rather than a way to earn or achieve power itself [1][3][5][6][16][18]. He emphasizes that the power of God is an inheritance for every born-again believer [1][16].

Here's more on what he teaches about prayer:
*   **Accessing and Releasing Power** Prayer is how believers access their spiritual office and position, and it puts the power of God to work and on display [6][11]. When we pray, we are making tremendous power available, dynamic in its working [7][13][15]. This power is already inside us, and prayer helps it come outside [11].
*   **Not for Earning Power** Rev. Peter clarifies that prayer does not *bring* power into a believer; the power is already there as a gift from God. The purpose of prayer, especially Paul's prayers, is for believers to come to *experience* and *know* the power they already have experientially, and to use it [1][3][5][16]. A prayerless Christian is not a powerless Christian, but one who has neglected the power by not praying [16].
*   **The Power of God's Word** The Word of God comes with power and authority, and as it comes, the power of God meets every need—for restoration, healing, and deliverance [2]. Rev. Peter encourages praying with serious intensity for the Word of God to meet these needs [2]. Your word is power, and God watches over His word to bring it to pass [8].
*   **Fasting and Prayer** Fasting, like prayer, doesn't *bring* power but *releases* it [18]. Combining fasting with prayer shows seriousness about a matter and allows your spirit to gain ascendancy, often resulting in answers quickly, sometimes before three days are up [18].
*   **Types of Prayer**
    *   **Prayer of Consecration** Rev. Peter teaches that the most powerful prayers are prayers of consecration, where a believer surrenders their will to God, saying, "Lord, whatever you want me to do, that's what I want to do" [9][10][12]. This helps align with God's will, which is good, perfect, and acceptable [12].
    *   **Praying in the Spirit and Understanding** It is important to pray in the spirit and in understanding [13]. Praying in the spirit involves divine utterance and is an access key to your spiritual office [6].
    *   **Persistent and Heartfelt Prayer** The heartfelt and persistent prayer of a righteous person can accomplish much and make tremendous power available [15]. When we pray with believing, things begin to happen, the enemy is wearied out, and we are strengthened [13].
*   **Practical Aspects of Prayer** To stay awake during prayer, especially for extended periods, it is helpful to pray out loud, pace the floor, and walk around [17].

You're looking for messages where Rev. Peter shares his university experiences, particularly carrying his keyboard to other fellowships to play. This powerful story is indeed found in several of his teachings.

Here are some messages where he discusses this:

*   **How GOD Calls and Why GOD Calls Into the Ministry** Rev. Peter recounts how he would joyfully borrow his fellowship's keyboard and himself to Kingsword fellowship, hoping Dr. K would notice him and impart something, but he was not seen at that time. He also explains that God's love for you isn't dependent on a minister recognizing you, as a minister's mental faculties can still escape the Holy Ghost's influence, citing Samuel missing David (1 Samuel 3:18) [1][15].
*   **Man as GOD Created** Rev. Peter shares that he was a music director on campus and would carry his fellowship's keyboard to play for Kingsword, often after exams to honor Dr. K. He always expected Dr. K to discern the anointing on him, but it "went on for years" without being noticed, yet he knew "there was something inside me" [7].
*   **How to Have a Great Year - Part 5** Rev. Peter explains that God told him to "serve them," so he would volunteer himself and his keyboard to play for other fellowships' meetings, even when he had no academic reason to be on campus. He never got to meet the founders, but the Lord told him He brought him there to serve the anointing, because "the anointing knows who is serving it" [3].
*   **Our Heritage of the Work of the Ministry** Rev. Peter recalls being made choir director and how the Lord told him to "stay and serve faithfully where they put you." He sought a preaching group in university but was not given the opportunity for four years until his final year. He emphasizes that "stay in your fellowship, serve them there" was one of the best counsels he ever received, teaching him meekness and "power under control" as training for pastoral ministry [11].
*   **Prayer Works** Rev. Peter shares that one of the first things he did in his family church was learn to play the keyboard, becoming useful and volunteering. He joined the choir and, being better, "displaced all the organist of the church" while still in secondary school. He states, "God will find you to the degree that you grow," and as he gave himself to his own development, he didn't need to fight for places in the church because they found him useful and an asset [6].

turns.answer:
Beloved, it's understandable to feel overwhelmed when facing difficulties in your finances and marriage, but be rest assured that God's word provides guidance and power for these areas of your life. The Lord shall supply all your needs according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus [2].

Here's what the messages teach about navigating these challenges:

**In Your Finances:**
*   **Avoid the love of money and be generous:** Rev. Peter teaches that the love of money is often the root cause of disputes between spouses. Instead, believers must practice not loving money, being generous with it, and being accountable as a steward of money [3].
*   **Know your financial status:** Just as a medical check-up helps you understand your health, a "marital checkup" or financial assessment helps you know your current financial standing. Your cash balance isn't your true financial status; rather, it's determined by how you are currently handling your money [14].
*   **Pray about everything, including finances:** Pastor Funlola Alabi emphasizes that nothing is too small or insignificant to pray about, including your finances [11]. When you pray, power is released immediately and goes into areas like your finances, marriage, business, and body [17].

**In Your Marriage:**
*   **Deal with strife and yield to the Holy Spirit:** Wherever there is strife, there is all manner of evil workings, and allowing strife in your marriage gives the devil an open door. If both spouses yield to the Holy Ghost, it shouldn't be difficult for them to live peaceably [3]. Quarrels should reduce as you grow [3].
*   **Prioritize your spouse and avoid harmful words:** Rev. Peter states that for a man, once married, his wife is priority over his mother [4]. It's crucial to be careful what you say to each other during disagreements, as negative words can block the blessings and support your spouse is meant to supply to your life [7]. Never say things like "you are good for nothing" or "I will bury you to the ground" to your spouse; instead, affirm that you "rise together" [7].
*   **Grow spiritually to overcome marital problems:** Many marital problems are solved when both spouses grow spiritually. If you commit to spiritual growth, much of your marital issues will diminish, because fights often stem from immaturity and the dominance of the flesh [13].
*   **Handle money with honesty and honor:**
    *   Nagging about finances or using manipulative tactics like hiding money or lying about prices is confusing emotions with facts and is not aligned with being a Christian [1][9]. If you have issues, talk about them directly and honestly, letting your husband know how you want to be included in financial decision-making [1].
    *   Avoid borrowing money from your spouse, as it can strain the relationship and create an open door for the enemy [6]. If a spouse has a financial need and you can meet it, do so with honor and speak words of affirmation, believing in them [12]. As a man, never complain about your wife not giving you money, as it's disgraceful to manhood [15].
*   **Beware of the "sin of neglect":** Guest minister Sola Babalola describes neglect as consciously or unconsciously disregarding your spouse's concerns or instructions. Many problems in marriage become crises because of this neglect [18].
*   **Make time for your spouse and balance work:** While a man needs to work to provide, there are times when work demands excess. The wisdom is to make up for that time. Wives should be wise enough to find that balance and not make their husbands feel bad for needing to work [16].
*   **Do not hide assets or live separately:** Hiding properties from each other means you are not truly one in marriage, but living a caricature of marriage. Similarly, living in separate states because you can't live peaceably together means you are deceiving yourselves about being married [9]. Hiding earnings or secretly buying properties out of distrust brings negative outcomes [10].

Remember, you are marvelously helped, and anything you tried before that didn't work, go and do it again because this time you are making progress by the Spirit of God [2].
suggestions: How to overcome strife in marriage
Understanding God's perspective on money
Praying effectively for breakthroughs

Yes, Rev. Peter has discussed Netflix in several messages, often cautioning against its potential to distract from spiritual focus and negatively influence behavior.

Here are some points he has made:

*   In **How GOD Calls and Why GOD Calls Into the Ministry-Part 2**, Rev. Peter teaches that watching Netflix when God speaks can cause God's voice to grow weaker and fade, likening Netflix to an "eraser" for divine instructions [15].
*   In **2nd Service**, he advises against binging on Netflix before bed, explaining that what you consume before sleeping influences your subconscious and can leave your spirit open to non-divine activities. He recommends spending the last two hours before sleep with divine things like reading the Bible or listening to messages instead [5].
*   In **Faith and Divine Leading - Part 3**, Rev. Peter warns that sitting down all day watching Netflix without exercise can lead to rising blood pressure and other health issues, emphasizing that this is not luxury but a path to sickness, and can be foolishness that opens doors for demons if it contradicts a confession of healing [9][10].
*   During **40 Dot Immersion**, he points out that having Netflix open while livestreaming a service can split one's attention, hindering spiritual growth by preventing full focus and order in one's life [4].
*   In **Ambidextrous Believers - Part 4**, Rev. Peter cautions against allowing stories watched on Netflix to negatively condition your behavior and responses, warning of "learned helplessness" and the importance of having "guts" in life [1].
*   He also brings up Netflix in **I Say This to Your Shame**, challenging believers that if they can pay monthly subscriptions for Netflix, they should be willing to invest in spiritual growth by buying resources like the Eword app [8][17].

Beloved, I can only provide insights from the church's messages. Based on what Rev. Peter teaches, faith is a vital, inherent possession for believers, given by God, through which we interact with Him and live a supernatural life.

Rev. Peter emphasizes that God is a "faith God" who speaks and expects manifestations, and we cannot relate to Him without faith [5][14]. He teaches that everything God requires of man, He also supplies to man, including faith [14]. This faith is an "eternal possession" that has been given to us; if you are in Christ, you have faith [5]. In fact, there is only one faith of God, not different kinds for men or women, pastors or members (Ephesians 4:5) [12]. You already have all the faith you ever need; the true challenge often isn't a lack of faith, but an abundance of unbelief [16].

Faith is not passive; it speaks, especially in the face of trials and tests [1]. As Psalm 116:8-10 declares, "I believed, therefore have I spoken. I was greatly afflicted" [1]. However, faith speaks to God and His Word, not to manipulate or pressure human beings. Rev. Peter warns against "stylish begging" or talking in a way that seeks pity from others; instead, we should talk to God secretly [1]. One of the beautiful outcomes of living by faith is that it dignifies our lives [1].

When it comes to putting faith to work, Rev. Peter teaches that "there is no faith that does not work. It was you that did not work," highlighting the importance of being well-schooled in how faith operates [6]. A common pitfall believers face is trying to determine *how* God will answer their faith. Rev. Peter explains that the "how" is beyond us, it is the exclusive domain of God because He has "more than 1 million and one ways to do one thing" [6].

He also stresses the importance of a "faith company"—people with whom you can discuss spiritual matters in faith, which helps bring clarity and light on what to do [8]. Such a company stands in contrast to a "fear company" that might deem your faith declarations too grand [8]. Ultimately, faith speaks, and then we act, becoming unstoppable because Satan "cannot stop a move of faith" as faith is "too strong for Satan to withstand" [8]. Therefore, we should act with intention and desire, believing that our prayers and actions release power and bring change (Mark 11:24) [9].

Additionally, Pastor Funlola Alabi teaches that the faith of God is a gift, not something earned, received through hearing and believing the Word of God (Romans 10:17) [10]. She explains that faith is crucial because it is how we understand God's work and scriptures (Hebrews 11:3) and how we are saved (Ephesians 2:8) [13].
